correctness.rationale: For fixed m=2r+1, precisely m unordered vertex pairs at step r maximize polygon diameter 2cos(pi/(2m)), and their vertices are shared. In each corner cone the two longest-diagonal inward loss forms have slopes (q,p) and (p,q), where p=sin(pi/(2m)), q=sin(3pi/(2m)), and the edge-coordinate area Jacobian divided by polygon area is exactly 2/m. After scaling corner coordinates by sqrt(N), disjoint vertex neighborhoods converge jointly to independent intensity-2/m Poisson processes. Strict first-order transversality and positive gap outside neighborhoods justify localization and a uniformly O(N^-1) Taylor remainder, giving weak convergence of the minimum over finite diameter pairs. The two directional minima at one vertex are dependent and their joint survival is the Poisson void probability for union of two triangles; direct trapezoidal/midpoint integration confirms all piecewise intersection formulas. Each one-diagonal sum has CDF lambda² t^4/6+O(t^6). Pairwise diagonal intersections require at least 3 corner processes and contribute O(t^6), so inclusion–exclusion gives m lambda²/6=1/(6mp²q²). Finally small-angle limits give 8/(27 pi^4) versus even 1/(12 pi^4), ratio 32/9. Independent checks of 5 vertex gradients and 600 exact-versus-quadrature overlaps are supplementary only.

value.rationale: Random-sample diameter is a canonical geometric extreme statistic. Odd regular polygons are the first natural symmetric class where maximal-diameter chords share endpoints, so the missing dependence invalidates naive products of independent Weibull variables. The bivariate cone process and exact lower-tail coefficient are nontrivial geometry-probability invariants, not a minor constant gain. The parity contrast quantifies an important structural distinction from even polygons.

final_claim: For fixed odd regular m-gon (m>=3, circumradius 1) and area-uniform iid N-sample, sqrt(N) times the diameter deficit converges in law to the minimum of m coupled sums U_j+V_(j+r), where each independent vertex Poisson process supplies the correlated pair U_j,V_j. Joint bivariate survival is explicit triangle-overlap exp(-lambda(s²+t²)+(2/m)I_(p,q)(s,t)); lower tail constant 1/(6m p²q²) gives odd/even large-m coefficient ratio 32/9 in successive limits.
